claims.claim: Rewriting in Go might make 400 ms into 100 ms (about 4x faster than the current Node/Express renderer)
claims.measured: CPU fib(20): go-gin 18,218 req/s, go-nethttp 15,093 vs node-express 7,213 (2.1–2.5x)
claims.why: The claimed 4x speedup is within a factor of 2 of the measured 2.1–2.5x advantage on the CPU-bound test.

claims.claim: Rewriting in Rust might make 400 ms into 100 ms (about 4x faster than Node)
claims.measured: CPU fib(20): rust-axum 29,499 req/s, rust-actix 26,886 vs node-express 7,213 (3.7–4.1x)
claims.why: The measured CPU-bound speedup over Express is about 4x, which matches the claim.

claims.claim: Rewriting in Java might make 400 ms into 100 ms (about 4x faster than Node)
claims.measured: CPU fib(20): java-spring 14,258 req/s, java-spring-vt 13,457 vs node-express 7,213 (1.9–2.0x)
claims.why: Java measured about 2x Express on CPU work, so the claimed 4x is too high but still only about 2x off, which is within the tolerance.

claims.claim: A 400 ms synchronous render inside the Express event loop blocks every other request on that process
claims.why: The benchmarks measure throughput for each workload on its own and never mix a long synchronous task with other requests, so they can't show the blocking effect.

claims.claim: Headless Chromium instances may need 300–500 MB of RAM each
claims.why: No Chromium or PDF-rendering server was benchmarked.
